sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:96
items.html:
Explains: why each and every Sefira is comprised of ten particular Sefirot, and the particular ones are comprised of ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars, and so they go on expanding without end or number. Every particular Sefira in every single world is comprised of ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars, etc., without end or number:

The matter of the division of the Sefirot into particulars and into particulars of particulars, without end.
This is a wondrous law in the upper worlds, that in every Sefira we choose to examine, we find in it ten particular Sefirot, and when we take once more a single Sefira from among those ten particular Sefirot, we likewise discern ten Sefirot that are particulars of particulars relative to the first Sefira, and so too, if we take a single Sefira from among the Sefirot of particulars of particulars, we again find in it ten Sefirot, which are particulars of the previous particulars of particulars, and so on without end.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:97
items.html:
Every light that passes through the degrees leaves its root in each and every degree through which it passed.
You will understand the reason for this from what has been explained, that there is no absence in spirituality (see Inner Light, Part 2, Chapter 1, item 4, second). It is explained there that it is utterly impossible to find any aspect of light in a lower being that is not likewise included in all the upper beings above it, up to Ein Sof. This is because even a very small illumination that emerges at the lowest degree in the worlds must come out from Ein Sof and pass through all the worlds and degrees that precede that lowest degree, until its arrival there. And since it is impossible that this illumination, as it cascades and passes through the degrees, should be absent from the first degree because of its arrival at the second, and be absent from the second when it arrives at the third, and so on until its arrival at the last degree that truly receives it — in the manner of a corporeal object passing from place to place — for this is utterly inconceivable in spiritual matters, where absence and change do not apply at all, it is necessarily so that any illumination that passes through some degree, even if it is only in passing, has nonetheless already acquired its place there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:98
items.html:
Any light that has once appeared at some degree never departs from there, forever.
And the matter of its arrival and its transfer to the degree that follows does not, on that account, diminish at all from the light that it left behind and that acquired its place in the degree it passed through; rather, this is like one who lights one candle from another, where the first is not diminished. So too here, at the time the light is transferred from the first degree and descends to the second, the whole light is found intact, both in the first and in the second. And in the same way, when the light arrives at the third degree, it does not depart from the second at all, and the light is found in its full completeness both in the second and in the third. And so it is as it passes through all the degrees that precede that final degree, which is the true recipient — that is, up to the degree for which the light descended from Ein Sof — it becomes fixed in all of them. All this is because absence does not apply in spirituality, and any light that has once shone in a spiritual aspect never departs from that aspect, forever, not even the tiniest fraction.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:99
items.html:
When the light of Hochma passes to its place through Keter, it leaves its root in Keter.
From what has been explained you will well understand the matter of the inclusion of the ten Sefirot in one another, without end. For example, when the first two Sefirot, Keter and Hochma, emerge, the light of Hochma must come out from Ein Sof, as above, and so the light of Hochma must pass through the Sefira of Keter before it arrives at the Sefira of Hochma. And since the light of Hochma has once shone in the Sefira of Keter, that is, at the time it passed through there, it is therefore impossible that it should ever be absent from there, as above. Accordingly, it is necessarily so that even after the light of Hochma has already reached the Sefira of Hochma, the light of Hochma remains in its completeness in Keter as well. Thus in the Sefira of Keter there are now two lights, namely, the light of Keter and the light of Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:100
items.html:
When the light of Bina passes through Keter and Hochma, it leaves its root in them. And so on, similarly.
Likewise with the light of Bina: since it must pass through the two preceding Sefirot before its arrival at the Sefira of Bina, it is necessarily so that the light of Bina acquired a place in both Keter and Hochma, as above. There are now three lights in Keter, namely: the light of Keter, the light of Hochma, and the light of Bina. And there are two lights in Hochma, namely: the light of Hochma and the light of Bina. And there is one light in the Sefira of Bina, namely, its own light. And so on in this manner, until, when the light of Malchut emerges, all ten Sefirot are already present in Keter, since all nine lower lights necessarily passed through Keter and therefore acquired their place there, as above. And there are nine Sefirot in Hochma, since all eight Sefirot below it necessarily passed through its place and remained there, as above. Likewise, there are eight Sefirot in Bina, seven in Hesed, six in Gevura, and so on down to Malchut, which has only its own light alone, since there is no Sefira beneath it that would pass through it.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:101
items.html:
There is no direct light in the vessel of Malchut, only reflected light.
However, the matter of the aforementioned light of Malchut — both the light within her and the light included from her in the first nine Sefirot — is nothing but reflected light. For you already know that from the restriction onward a screen came into being in the Sefira of Malchut, and the light of Ein Sof is not received there; rather, something is made there, by virtue of the meeting of the light of Ein Sof with that screen, a matter of coupling, and then a new light emerges and rises from the screen in Malchut, called reflected light, and it illuminates up to the Sefira of Keter above, and is thus found to clothe, from below upward, all ten Sefirot in their entirety. Only in this way is she found included in each Sefira of the first nine Sefirot (as stated above, Inner Observation, Part 2, item 19, sub header, “Now”).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:102
items.html:
Malchut is considered the Keter of the ten Sefirot of reflected light.
Since the Sefira of Malchut is the source of that new light, and every source is considered to be called Keter, Malchut is therefore considered the Sefira of Keter of that new light. And the Sefira before it, namely Yesod, is considered the Hochma of the new light, and the one before that, namely Hod, is considered the Bina, until the upper Keter is now considered in the aspect of Malchut, namely, in the aspect of what it receives from that new light.

The ten Sefirot of direct light go from above downward.
Now, it has been explained that we must discern, at every degree of ten Sefirot, that there are there two orders of ten Sefirot: namely, the order of ten Sefirot extending from Ein Sof, from above downward, from Keter to Malchut, which are called the ten Sefirot of direct light, since they descend in straightness from above downward, according to the order of the degree — that is, from the refined vessel to the one coarser than it, and from there to the still coarser one, until Malchut, the coarsest of all.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:103
items.html:
The ten Sefirot of reflected light go from below upward.
And there is also there a second order of ten Sefirot, extending from the Sefira of Malchut, from below upward, that is, from the Sefira of Malchut to the Sefira of Keter, since Malchut becomes the source of this new light; and these are called the ten Sefirot of reflected light. They are so called because they are conveyed and come in the reverse of the order of the degree — that is, it does not extend and go from the refined vessel to the coarse one, where the final recipient is the coarsest, but rather the opposite: it extends and goes from the coarsest vessel to one that is not as coarse, until the final recipient is the most refined of all. Therefore it is said to illuminate from below upward.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:104
items.html:
All the Sefirot of reflected light that come in the nine Sefirot of direct light pass through Malchut.
Now, the matter of the inclusion of the Sefirot that we explained above concerning the order of the ten Sefirot of direct light — that by virtue of the fact that there is no absence in spirituality, and any illumination that passes through a place remains there in its full completeness even after it has moved on to a second place, and it is for this reason that, in the emergence of the ten Sefirot of direct light, all ten Sefirot are found to be present in Keter, nine in Hochma, eight in Bina, and so on (as above, item 99, sub header “From what has been explained,” see there) — for that very same reason it is likewise found regarding the ten Sefirot of reflected light. Since it is here that the Sefira of Malchut becomes the aspect of the source for this reflected light, it is thus found for us that any aspect of reflected light that reaches the Sefirot above it must necessarily pass through the place of Malchut, since it is Malchut that brings forth that aspect of light, by virtue of her screen, which couples with the light of Ein Sof that strikes that screen.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:105
items.html:
When the reflected light of Yesod passes through Malchut, it leaves its root in Malchut, and so on, similarly.
Therefore, when the Sefira of Yesod receives its reflected light from Malchut, this light was necessarily received by Malchut beforehand, through the coupling with the light of Ein Sof, and it passed through Malchut and came to the Sefira of Yesod. Thus the light of Yesod is found both in Malchut and in Yesod. Likewise with the aspect of reflected light received by Hod, which necessarily acquired its place, in passing, both in Malchut and in Yesod; and there are now three lights in Malchut, two lights in Yesod, and one light in Hod. And so on, until the last aspect of reflected light, received by Keter, at which point there are already found in Malchut ten lights of the ten Sefirot of reflected light, in Yesod nine lights, in Hod eight lights, and so on, in the manner explained regarding the ten Sefirot of direct light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:106
items.html:
Through the inclusion of reflected light by way of passage, ten Sefirot became fixed in each and every Sefira. In Keter there are nine Sefirot of direct light, and one of reflected light.
Therefore it results for us that there are ten Sefirot in each and every Sefira of the aforementioned ten Sefirot, that is, in combination with the reflected light. In other words, the light of Malchut received in each and every Sefira is what completes it to ten Sefirot. For in Keter there are nine Sefirot of direct light — Keter, Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod — and one Sefira of reflected light, which is Malchut, since she is the final recipient of the ten Sefirot of reflected light, as above, and therefore it has only one light of reflected light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:107
items.html:
In Hochma there are eight of direct light, and two of reflected light. In Bina there are seven of direct light, and three of reflected light.
Hochma has eight Sefirot of direct light, namely: Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod, and two Sefirot of reflected light, namely: one part of itself, which it received from the reflected light of Malchut, which is the Yesod of reflected light, and the second is the part of Keter that passed through it and no longer departed from there, which is the Malchut of reflected light, as above. And Bina has seven lights of direct light, namely: Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod, and three Sefirot of reflected light, namely: Hod, Yesod, Malchut — Hod of its own, Yesod from the part of Hochma that passed through it, Malchut from the part of Keter that passed through it, that is, from Bina and above, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:108
items.html:
In Hesed there are six of direct light, and four of reflected light. In Gevura there are five of direct light, and five of reflected light. In Tifferet there are four of direct light and six of reflected light.
Hesed has six Sefirot of direct light, namely: Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod. And four Sefirot of reflected light, from Hesed and above, namely, its own part, which is Netzah, and the parts of Bina, Hochma, and Keter, which are Hod, Yesod, and Malchut, that passed through it and became fixed there, as above. Likewise, Gevura has five Sefirot of direct light, namely: Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod. And five Sefirot of reflected light, from Gevura and above, namely, the four parts of Keter, Hochma, Bina, and Hesed, which are Netzah, Hod, Yesod, and Malchut, that passed through it, and its own part, which is the Tifferet of reflected light. And Tifferet has four Sefirot of direct light, namely, from Tifferet downward. And six Sefirot of reflected light, from Tifferet and above, namely, the five parts of Keter, Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura, which are Netzah, Hod, Yesod, Malchut, that passed through it, and its own part, which is the Gevura of reflected light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:109
items.html:
In Netzah there are three of direct light, and seven of reflected light. In Hod there are two of direct light and eight of reflected light. In Yesod there are nine of reflected light and one of direct light. And Malchut has ten Sefirot of reflected light.
Netzah has three Sefirot of direct light, from Netzah downward, namely Netzah, Hod, Yesod of direct light. And seven Sefirot of reflected light, from Netzah and above, namely the six parts of Keter, Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet that passed through it, which are Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod, Malchut of reflected light, and its own part, which is the Hesed of reflected light. Hod has two Sefirot of direct light: Hod and Yesod, and eight Sefirot of reflected light, from Hod and above, namely the seven parts of Keter, Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah that passed through it, which are Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod, Malchut of reflected light, and its own part, which is the Bina of reflected light. And Yesod has one Sefira of direct light, and nine Sefirot of reflected light, from Yesod and above, namely the eight parts of Keter, Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod that passed through it, which are Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod, Malchut of reflected light, and its own part, which is the Hochma of reflected light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:110
items.html:
Malchut, through her reflected light, completes each and every Sefira to ten.
Now, it has been thoroughly explained that in every manifestation of the ten Sefirot, wherever they may be, they must include one another the moment the ten Sefirot of direct light emerge. However, there are not yet ten Sefirot in each one of them, until the light of Malchut — that is, the ten Sefirot of reflected light — is also included in them, since she has no other light, as above. And this light of Malchut completes the missing part of the number ten for each and every one of the ten Sefirot, until ten Sefirot are found in each and every one of them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:111
items.html:
And so it is with the particulars of particulars. When you take the Keter of the ten Sefirot within Keter, it likewise necessarily has nine Sefirot of direct light and one of reflected light.
Now, if you take, for example, the general Sefira of Keter from among the aforementioned general ten Sefirot, which is itself already comprised of particular ten Sefirot, as above, that is, after the light of Malchut has been revealed there, you must immediately understand that in the first Sefira of that general Keter, now called the Keter of Keter, that is, the particular Keter, it is necessarily comprised of the nine Sefirot of direct light found beneath it, namely Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod of direct light that are in Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:112
items.html:
The Keter of Keter is the aspect of itself, and the nine lower Sefirot are lights in passage.
And although only the Keter among them is the aspect of itself, the other nine particular Sefirot within it are not so, but rather aspects of lights in passage, that is, lower lights that acquired their place there in passing, from Ein Sof to the Sefirot lower than Keter. Nevertheless, since they are found within Keter, it is necessarily so that the uppermost Sefira, which is the particular Keter among them, also now includes, by itself, the nine particular Sefirot found beneath it. For since these nine Sefirot too are found beneath it, they necessarily passed through it, and since they passed through it, they necessarily acquired their place within it, since there is no absence in spirituality, exactly as above regarding the general ten Sefirot. In this way, there are now found in this particular Keter, by itself, likewise ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars, namely, nine of direct light — Keter, Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod — and one of reflected light, which is the light of Malchut, as above regarding the Keter of the general ten Sefirot.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:113
items.html:
Likewise, Hochma within Keter necessarily has eight Sefirot of direct light and two of reflected light.
In exactly the same way, when you take to examine the particular Sefira of Hochma among the particular ten Sefirot of the aforementioned general Keter, called Hochma of Keter, it necessarily now has ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars, in the manner stated above regarding the particular Keter. For all eight particular Sefirot of direct light of the general Keter that are found beneath it necessarily passed through that particular Hochma, from above downward, and since they passed through it, they necessarily acquired their place within it. And there are also two more Sefirot of reflected light, namely from the light of the particular Malchut, which likewise passed through that particular Hochma, from below upward, namely: the part of reflected light of its own, and the part of reflected light belonging to the particular Keter. Thus there are ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars also in the particular Hochma within the particular ten Sefirot of the general Keter, in the same manner as in the general Hochma within the general ten Sefirot.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:114
items.html:
Likewise, Bina within Keter has seven Sefirot of direct light and three of reflected light.
In exactly the same way, when you take to examine the particular Bina among the particular ten Sefirot of the general Keter, called Bina of Keter, you will likewise find that it necessarily now has ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars, as was explained regarding the particular Hochma above. For all six particular Sefirot — Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod of direct light of the general Keter — that are found beneath it necessarily passed, from above downward, through that particular Bina, and acquired their place within it; these are now, together with Bina itself, seven Sefirot of direct light. And likewise, three particular Sefirot of reflected light passed through that Bina, from the particular Malchut of the general Keter, from below upward, namely: the part of reflected light of its own, the part of reflected light of the particular Hochma, and the part of reflected light of the particular Keter. Thus there are ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars in the particular Bina within the ten Sefirot of the general Keter, just as stated regarding the general Bina within the general ten Sefirot.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:115
items.html:
Likewise, Hesed within Keter has six Sefirot of direct light and four of reflected light. And so on, similarly.
In exactly the same way, you will find ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars in the particular Hesed within the particular ten Sefirot of the general Keter, namely six of direct light — Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod — from above downward, and four of reflected light, from Hesed and above up to Keter. And in exactly the same way, you will find ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars in Gevura, and so on, down to the particular Malchut within those ten Sefirot, called Malchut of Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:116
items.html: One should not raise the difficulty that in the aforementioned particular ten Sefirot of the general Keter there is, of the reflected light that rose from the general Malchut, only the aspect of Nefesh — namely, the last part of reflected light, the smallest of all the ten Sefirot of reflected light, as above (item 112, sub header “And although”) — and how then can we say that this small part of reflected light now expands, by itself, into new ten Sefirot of reflected light, so as to complete, for each particular Sefira, all the Sefirot of particulars of particulars that they lack to reach the count of ten Sefirot.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:117
items.html:
The Nefesh of reflected light within the general Keter necessarily divides so as to clothe the ten particular Sefirot within Keter.
The answer, however, is that ultimately it is necessarily so that that part of the particular Nefesh of reflected light, which rose from Malchut to the general Keter, sufficed to clothe there all nine particular Sefirot found in the general Keter. For if it were not so, these nine Sefirot of direct light would not be grasped and would not illuminate in the Partzuf at all, since, as is known, there is no possibility for direct light to be bound in a Partzuf except by means of the aspect of the vessel of reception of reflected light, as above. And since this light of Nefesh clothed the nine particular Sefirot in Keter, it is necessarily so that, by way of passage from below upward, it completed for each and every one of those particular Sefirot the number of Sefirot of particulars of particulars that it lacked. For to Hochma it gave the two lights it lacked: one light to clothe itself, and a second light, in passing, to clothe Keter. And to Bina, three; and to Hesed, four, as has been explained above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:118
items.html:
Likewise with the ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars in the general Hochma. In the Keter of particulars of particulars within Hochma there are nine Sefirot of direct light and one of reflected light.
In the same manner that the ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars were explained regarding the ten particular Sefirot of the general Keter, in exactly that same manner the ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars are explained in each and every one of the ten particular Sefirot of the general Sefira of Hochma. For in the Keter of the ten particular Sefirot of the general Hochma, called Keter of Hochma, you will necessarily find ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars, namely: its own particular light, and the eight particular Sefirot Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod that passed through it from above downward — that makes nine — and one of reflected light that rose to it from the particular Malchut of the general Hochma. Thus you have ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars in the Keter of the general Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:119
items.html:
In the Hochma of particulars of particulars within Hochma there are eight of direct light and two of reflected light.
And so too with the particular Hochma within the particular ten Sefirot of the general Hochma, called Hochma of Hochma: it has eight of direct light from above downward, and two of reflected light from below upward. Likewise, the particular Bina within the particular ten Sefirot of the general Hochma has seven of direct light from above downward, and three of reflected light from below upward. And so too with Hesed, and so too with Gevura, and so on, down to the particular Malchut within those ten Sefirot of the general Hochma, called Malchut of Hochma, which likewise has ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars of reflected light — that is, by virtue of the fact that it necessarily clothes all the particular ten Sefirot of the general Hochma and sends them its illuminations, as above, so that they are necessarily found to have all passed through it and acquired their place within it, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:120
items.html: In exactly the same manner, the particular Bina is considered to have its own ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars. And so too the particular Hesed, and the particular Gevura, down to the particular Malchut, and there is no need to elaborate on this further. Rather, let us explain one more Sefira of particulars of particulars, to show how it too, by itself, is considered, by that very same necessity, as ten Sefirot in its own right, which are now particular ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:121
items.html: And when we take to examine the Bina of particulars of particulars, which is, for example, one Sefira from among the ten Sefirot of particulars of particulars found in the particular Hochma within the ten Sefirot of the general Hochma, called Bina within Hochma of Hochma, you will likewise find in it, by itself, ten Sefirot, in the same manner as above, namely seven of direct light that passed through it from above downward, and three of reflected light that passed through it from below upward.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:122
items.html: And in this way, one can go on detailing and discerning without any real end whatsoever, since always, if you take any Sefira, even after the thousandth instance of detailing, you have taken that Sefira from within an order of ten Sefirot, and so it is necessarily so that part of those ten Sefirot passed through that Sefira from above downward, and part of them passed through it from below upward, whereby those ten Sefirot necessarily acquired their place in that Sefira eternally, as above. Thus you necessarily have all ten Sefirot in that Sefira. Understand this well.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:123
items.html: However, you should understand that although you go on detailing from ten to ten, and the second ten into thirds, and so on, do not imagine that all the Sefirot remain equal; rather, they go on changing greatly in the course of their detailing, and one is not equal to another. This is because the lights of direct light always come out of their place in the course of the detailing in all the Sefirot, except in Keter. For in Hochma, there is nothing there but eight of direct light — that is, from Hochma downward — and two of reflected light, Yesod and Malchut. So the eight lights of direct light come into the aspect of the most refined vessels, as above, namely from Keter to Hod, and the two of reflected light come into Yesod and Malchut. Thus the light of Hochma comes in the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina in the vessel of Hochma, and so on, until the light of Yesod comes in the vessel of Hod. Thus all the lights of direct light come out of their place, but only the reflected light always comes in its own place, since the reflected light of Yesod comes in the vessel of Yesod, and the reflected light of Malchut in the vessel of Malchut of Malchut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:124
items.html: And so too with Bina, which has only seven lights of direct light, which are received in the most refined vessels, as above, since every recipient receives in the most refined thing — that is, from Keter to Netzah. Thus the light of Bina is found in the vessel of Keter, and the light of Hesed in Hochma, down to the light of Yesod in the vessel of Netzah; only the three lights of reflected light come in their own place: the lights of Hod, Yesod, and Malchut, in the vessels of Hod, Yesod, and Malchut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:125
items.html: According to what has been explained, there is a great difference between the particular Bina of Keter, the particular Bina of Hochma, and the particular Bina of Bina, and so on. For only in the Bina of Keter is the light of Bina found in its own vessel; whereas in the Bina of Hochma, there is nothing there but the light of Hesed in the vessel of Bina. And in the Bina of Bina, there is nothing there but the light of Gevura in the vessel of Bina, and so with all of them. Thus one is not like another.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:126
items.html: And even the lights of reflected light, which do not change their place, as above, nevertheless one can discern changes in them as well in the course of the detailing, since wherever the reflected light is, it is found that an illumination of direct light expands to it. Therefore, for example, in the Yesod of Hochma, an illumination expands to it from the direct light of Hod of Hochma; whereas in the Yesod of Bina, an illumination expands to it from Netzah of Bina, since in the Hod of Bina there is no direct light, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 9:127
items.html: However, an exception to the aforementioned rule is this: if you take care to detail only the same general Sefira exclusively — I mean, if you take, for example, the general Sefira of Bina, and go on detailing it from ten to ten, that is, for example, you detail the particular-of-particular Bina from among the ten Sefirot of the particular Bina of the general ten Sefirot of Bina, called Bina of Bina of Bina — then they will all be equal to one another without any difference at all. For in all of them you will find seven of direct light in the seven upper vessels, Keter, Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, and three of reflected light in the three lower vessels, Hod, Yesod, Malchut, and so it remains even after the thousandth instance of detailing, and so too with the rest of the Sefirot.
